sources.title: MuJoCo Menagerie: Unitree G1 model
sources.specific_reference: Pinned unitree_g1/scene.xml and unitree_g1/g1.xml, standard rev_1_0 configuration: one free base, 29 actuated hinge joints, position actuators, left_foot and right_foot sites, pelvis and torso IMUs, and non-articulated left_rubber_hand and right_rubber_hand meshes. This record establishes the exact canonical morphology only; it supplies no task score.

sources.title: HumanoidBench: Simulated Humanoid Benchmark for Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation
sources.specific_reference: Paper Section III identifies Unitree H1 with two Shadow Hands as the primary benchmark robot; Section IV-A and Appendix B-E define walk, stand, run, reach, hurdle, crawl, maze, sit, balance, stair, slide, pole, and push; Figure 3 states that episode returns sum all timestep rewards and its dashed lines indicate task success. At the pinned revision, tasks.py defines the default 1000-step horizon and __init__.py registers each task with its declared max_episode_steps. The repository's later auxiliary G1 adaptation reports dof 44 in robots.py and 37 task actuators in assets/robots/g1_torque.xml lines 369-411, including fourteen articulated-hand motors; it is not treated as the paper's primary source robot or as the canonical Menagerie configuration. envs/basic_locomotion_envs.py, envs/reach.py, envs/maze.py, envs/balance.py, envs/pole.py, and envs/push.py contain the exact reward, endpoint, horizon, and success_bar definitions used clause by clause below. Exact public fixture geometry comes from assets/tasks/hurdle.xml, crawl.xml, maze.xml, sit_simple.xml, balance_simple.xml, stair.xml, slide.xml, pole.xml, and push.xml plus assets/locomotion/generated_xml_hurdles.xml, generated_xml_maze.xml, generated_xml_stairs.xml, and generated_xml_poles.xml at the same pinned revision.

sources.title: RoboCup Soccer Humanoid League Laws of the Game 2025
sources.specific_reference: Rules-Core.tex Section III includes moving-ball.tex, parkour.tex, high-kick.tex, obstacle_navigation.tex, and long-stride.tex. Section_I/law4.tex lines 65-66 classify 100-200 cm robots as AdultSize. Section_I/law1.tex lines 98-103, 155-158, and 192-207 defines the approximately 14 by 9 m AdultSize field, 2.1 m penalty mark, and 2.6 by 1.8 m goal opening; Section_I/law2.tex lines 15-21 specifies a FIFA size 5 AdultSize ball. Section_III/general-rules.tex lines 39-69 defines the 25 minute limit and no-handler-interaction rule. Each included challenge file defines its setup, full-success event, repetitions, and ranking quantities. Push recovery was reviewed but excluded from this catalog because its stable-walking judgment is not fully machine-expressible without an unsupported numeric adaptation.

sources.specific_reference: envs/engine.py lines 96-118 defines the 1000-step episode default; lines 1196-1209 defines Goal success as robot-goal planar distance at most goal_size and Button success as contact between the selected button and any robot geom. envs/suite.py lines 99 and 108-152 defines Goal0 on [-1,1]^2 with goal_size 0.3 m; lines 164-214 defines Button0 with four radius-0.1 m buttons and 0.2 m keepout.
